comments.author: @MixyWixyTGV
comments.text: During the plandemic, and sick AF, my landlord who had already raised the rent by $200 "to save the house from having to be sold" decided to sell the house I was renting. Rent had jumped so high that I could get a place but I would have to downsize severely and put things in storage. I couldn't afford both storage and rent, so my friend and I decided to live in the car, put everything in storage, and look for a place that met our size requirements and budget. Nearly 8 months later, yes 8 months!! Of searching rental listings within 50 miles of the town we lived in and were tied to, we decided to get a bus and built it out. It wasnt one of those fancy things you see in videos, but it worked. We moved to the only place that allowed busses, a meth camping/trailer park on the outskirts of town. We continued to look for rentals but rent for a three bedroom was up by $1k a month in the area. It was estimated that the county saw 15% of the people go homeless during all that. We met so many people that were homeless, living in their cars, rvs, sheds, and garages during that time. He volunteered at a local food bank and the volume of people tripled in a year. We all seemed to move together before we found the campground, to public parking places, Cracker Barrel, and side streets. You cant stay in one place for more than a couple days before the cops tell you to move. It got so bad that ofter a year in the meth park we moved to a different state, leaving behind the town I had made home for over 15 years. What is happening in the US is more dire than people realize. Especially for elderly and disabled. Nobody counts the dead or covers this in journalism.
